verdict.title: Improve performance by caching Path objects and target type lookups
verdict.reason: The changes introduce caching mechanisms to `Path.from_text` and `TargetRegistry._get_target_type` to improve performance. The provided fail-to-pass test specifically verifies the caching behavior of `Path.from_text`, which was failing due to the absence of this caching. The new performance test file (`perf_report.py`) and the commit message indicate a broader performance optimization effort. A solver can understand the objective of performance improvement and implement the caching logic based on the described problem and the existing test failure.
verdict.statement: The `glom` library can be slow when repeatedly creating `Path` objects from the same text specifications, as each creation involves parsing the text. To improve performance, `Path` objects should be cached. This caching mechanism has a configurable maximum size, defined by `_MAX_CACHE`, to manage memory usage. Additionally, looking up target types for operations can be inefficient and should be memoized. Implementing these caching strategies would reduce redundant processing and speed up common operations.
